summary: npm package auto-executes bundled Windows RAT binary on install
details: retracfix@1.0.3 is a Windows-pinned npm package (os: win32) with no README, empty description, and no source code — its only functional content is a bundled Windows PE at bin/ezfn.exe and a two-line postinstall runner. The declared postinstall script (node postinstall.js) enumerates bin/ for any.exe and executes the first one via execFileSync on every install, so npm install triggers the binary automatically on any Windows host. The generic exe-picker wrapper hides the specific payload name from static inspection. bin/ezfn.exe is a.NET (VB.NET) PE whose symbol set is consistent with a Windows remote-access trojan / bot family: System.Net.Sockets with ClientSocket / ConnectServer / BeginConnect / ActivatePong / SendBot / ChatID (C2 client), Antivirus / Exclusion (AV-evasion), Spread (propagation), LoggerPath (keylogging/log staging), RegistryProxy / get_CurrentUser (registry persistence under HKCU), WebClient.DownloadString (secondary payload fetch), CreateDecryptor / CipherMode (encrypted C2 or stored-config decryption), avicap32.dll (webcam capture), and ManagementObjectSearcher (WMI host reconnaissance). Installing the package on Windows results in remote operator control of the installer's machine, credential and host reconnaissance, and persistence.
